take:
Creators here use Blender mostly as the place where other systems land. Ian Hubert (@ianhubertz) shows physics-driven flight: active and passive rigid bodies, hinge and spring constraints, and a linear motor constraint acting as a thruster, with custom properties wired through drivers for throttle and lights ([rigid-body spaceship](/e/DacssZfNGNS)). Other posts treat Blender as an import target. ZOZO's open-source cloth and soft-body solver ships a Blender plugin ([PPF Contact Solver](/e/DYuY_-7Oqk4)), FreeMoCap exports webcam motion capture to Blender, Unity and Unreal ([FreeMoCap](/e/DYAI_fCuvrY)), and a DuckStation fork dumps PS1 scenes as OBJ files that drop into Blender with positions intact ([PS1 rips](/e/DbqLB-zMoJR)).

The newest thread is Blender driven by AI agents instead of by hand. One demo pairs Blender MCP with Tripo to turn a 2D reference image into an arranged 3D scene ([Blender MCP + Tripo](/e/DHoPsMOxIRl)). @chase.h.ai had Codex model a hero asset through a repo of Blender skills without ever opening Blender, then embed it with Three.js, flagging mobile performance as the thing to check ([Codex + Blender](/e/DdUyTAAJTj6)). @nateherkai had Claude write a Python script that builds and animates the scene; Blender rendered 360 frames on GPU in about 15 minutes and FFmpeg stitched them ([Blender as code](/e/DeuZ4BnhCqA)). Both of those guides are comment-gated, so the posts show results more than full method.

Unreal Engine shows up in 4 of these posts, Unity in 2 and Claude Code in 2, usually as parallel export targets or as the agent at the controls. Several saves are silent showcases of painterly or ink-brush looks with no breakdown ([ink brush](/e/DNIYfXvsrTe)), and a weekly news roundup and a sponsored Higgsfield post mention Blender only in passing ([news roundup](/e/DbIxSSaEtGd)). The motion-capture thread continues in [One dancer, a thousand bodies](/guides/one-dancer-thousand-bodies). It suits 3D artists, technical animators and people wiring AI or capture pipelines into a renderer.
